pr.title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
pr.body: On some machines the EC reports a bogus but numeric current. My MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI+ (BAT1 BIF0_9) reports current_now=-65A for a ~7.5W discharge, so the panel showed Discharging -1124W while UPower correctly reported 7.5W. The sysfs override only guarded readability, so any numeric value clobbered the good UPower rate. This: - only trusts sysfs reads that succeed and are numeric (allows negative current_now, which is the normal discharging sign), - rejects insane magnitudes (>150W) or values wildly above UPower's rate (>3x when UPower is solid), keeping the UPower value instead, - displays the rate as magnitude (state already says charging/discharging, so no more -1124W), - compares idle against magnitude so a large negative rate can't fake charge-idle, - omits cycle_count 0 when UPower reports charge-cycles N/A so the panel shows — instead of a misleading 0. Complements #12649/#12755 (those cover failed/empty reads); this covers bogus-but-numeric reads. Verified with the extended battery-status-test.sh scenarios (bogus -65A, non-numeric, sane negative discharge) plus live hardware: bogus -1113W discharge now shows 7.5W, and a sane 29.1W charge still uses the live sysfs value.

pr.title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
pr.body: On some machines the EC reports a bogus but numeric current. My MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI+ (BAT1 BIF0_9) reports current_now=-65A for a ~7.5W discharge, so the panel showed Discharging -1124W while UPower correctly reported 7.5W. The sysfs override only guarded readability, so any numeric value clobbered the good UPower rate. This: - only trusts sysfs reads that succeed and are numeric (allows negative current_now, which is the normal discharging sign), - rejects insane magnitudes (>150W) or values wildly above UPower's rate (>3x when UPower is solid), keeping the UPower value instead, - displays the rate as magnitude (state already says charging/discharging, so no more -1124W), - compares idle against magnitude so a large negative rate can't fake charge-idle, - omits cycle_count 0 when UPower reports charge-cycles N/A so the panel shows — instead of a misleading 0. Complements #12649/#12755 (those cover failed/empty reads); this covers bogus-but-numeric reads. Verified with the extended battery-status-test.sh scenarios (bogus -65A, non-numeric, sane negative discharge) plus live hardware: bogus -1113W discharge now shows 7.5W, and a sane 29.1W charge still uses the live sysfs value.

pr.title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
pr.body: On some machines the EC reports a bogus but numeric current. My MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI+ (BAT1 BIF0_9) reports current_now=-65A for a ~7.5W discharge, so the panel showed Discharging -1124W while UPower correctly reported 7.5W. The sysfs override only guarded readability, so any numeric value clobbered the good UPower rate. This: - only trusts sysfs reads that succeed and are numeric (allows negative current_now, which is the normal discharging sign), - rejects insane magnitudes (>150W) or values wildly above UPower's rate (>3x when UPower is solid), keeping the UPower value instead, - displays the rate as magnitude (state already says charging/discharging, so no more -1124W), - compares idle against magnitude so a large negative rate can't fake charge-idle, - omits cycle_count 0 when UPower reports charge-cycles N/A so the panel shows — instead of a misleading 0. Complements #12649/#12755 (those cover failed/empty reads); this covers bogus-but-numeric reads. Verified with the extended battery-status-test.sh scenarios (bogus -65A, non-numeric, sane negative discharge) plus live hardware: bogus -1113W discharge now shows 7.5W, and a sane 29.1W charge still uses the live sysfs value.

pr.title: Keep UPower rate when sysfs power read fails with ENODEV
pr.body: Single-battery HP/ACPI machines expose a `power_now` that passes `[[ -r ]]` but whose `read()` fails with `ENODEV`, so the script gets `""` and `awk` coerces it to `0W`, discarding UPower's correct `energy-rate` (~16-30W). Only trust numeric sysfs reads, otherwise keep UPower's `energy-rate`. Same guard for the `current_now`/`voltage_now` fallback, which had the identical coerce-to-0 hole. Split out from #6845 per @bjarneo's request — that PR grew to cover 3 failure modes and was closed as a dup of #10392, which only handles multi-battery percentage and keeps this bug. This is the minimal fix for #6895 with regression tests for both empty-read cases. Fixes #6895. Extracted from #6845 (`3c40745`). Verified: existing `battery-status-test.sh` + 2 new ENODEV cases pass.

pr.title: Install stock kernel headers for broadcom-wl-dkms on upgraded Macs
pr.body: Arch dropped the prebuilt `broadcom-wl` on 2026-09-02, and `broadcom-wl-dkms` carries `replaces=(broadcom-wl)`. On an upgrade, pacman swaps the package in and pulls `dkms`, but nothing pulls `linux-headers`, so the module never builds: ``` running '70-dkms-install.hook'... ==> ERROR: Missing 7.2.3-arch1-3 kernel headers for module broadcom-wl/6.30.223.271. ``` 2012-2015 MacBooks with a BCM4360 or BCM4331 then come back from the Quattro upgrade with no driver bound and no Wi-Fi device at all. The installer's `fix-bcm43xx.sh` never runs on those machines, and `1789444024` only covers `linux-omarchy` and `linux-t2`. `1789325478` will give `linux-omarchy` its headers, but it deliberately leaves the stock kernel installed as the boot fallback. On these Macs that fallback still has no Wi-Fi, which is usually the way back to a working system. This migration installs headers for any installed Arch kernel (`linux`, `linux-lts`, `linux-zen`, `linux-hardened`) when `broadcom-wl-dkms` is present.
